decisions.statement: A change is a base commit and the rows the change states.
One array carries every row whether that row writes or takes away or moves.
The body a row leaves is worked out here rather than handed in beside the row.
A row appending is worked out against the body its path holds on the tree.
Rows appending to one path leave the content of every one of those rows.
One body is written for a path however many rows the change has for it.
A change stating no row is done rather than refused.
Such a change writes nothing and commits nothing and takes no hold.
A body the change does not touch is read from the base commit rather than from the working tree.
The bodies the change does not touch are read through one git process for the whole judging.
That git process is ended when the judging ends however the judging ends.
A change may state the commit its bodies were read against.
A name resolving to no commit refuses the change unwritten.
A path that moved between that commit and now is refused unwritten rather than written over.
A commit landing elsewhere in the repository moves no path this change has.
A change stating no commit the change was read against is taken as read against the commit at HEAD.
A body that moved is refused unwritten.
That refusal names the drop that takes away only the paths that moved.
The bodies written are put back when anything after the writing throws.
The bodies put back are the base commit's bodies.
The index is put back with the bodies.
The paths staged for a commit that threw are unstaged with the bodies.
A repair that fails leaves the fault that caused the repair to be thrown.
A repair that fails is said along with the fault that caused the repair.
A path the repository ignores is written after the commit lands.
A landing that throws writes no path the repository ignores.
A landing that throws puts back the paths that landing commits alone.
The body an ignored path already held stands where a landing throws.
A path the repository ignores that is written is answered as neither written nor taken.
A path the repository ignores that is taken away is answered on its own.
That answer is what says a removal no commit holds happened at all.
A landing that finishes unlinks every name it renamed aside.
The names renamed aside are unlinked before the folders are cleared.
A landing that throws between the rename and the unlink puts each body back where it came from.
An ignored path written over before a landing throws keeps the body that landing wrote.
A landing is finished after its commit rather than before that commit.
A change that commits nothing is finished all the same.
A landing that throws is finished by nothing.
A landing answers what its finishing cleared, linked, placed and kept.
A link outside the repository is placed outside the writing this refuses.
A hold runs from the first write to the commit.
A hold is kept while a repair waits on the git index.
A change is judged before the hold is taken.
The face saying which paths a machine writes is handed in rather than built inside the hold.
A landing handed no such face builds one inside the hold.
The ceiling on the call's seconds ends where the hold is taken.
A landing past the hold is left to finish however long that landing takes.
A change is judged against the commit the change read rather than the commit the change lands on.
A caller that worked the change out hands that change in rather than having it built again.
A change handed in is taken as worked out against the commit this landing judges.
A commit landing while a change is judged does not refuse that change.
A change that never took the hold is refused unwritten.
A landing that throws before the commit has committed nothing.
A landing that throws after the commit leaves that commit where it landed.
Such a landing puts the bodies back to the base commit's while HEAD keeps the commit it made.
A commit that landed is never answered as nothing.
A landing names the commit that landing landed in a slot the caller hands in.
A landing names that commit on the caller's list as prose rather than as a bare token.
A landing that committed nothing names nothing on that list or in that slot.
The index is settled before the commit.
Every commit this writes carries the attribution.
A body reaches disk only after every check has passed.
A path landing outside the repository refuses the change unwritten.
A move's two paths are weighed against the repository root as an edit's path is.
Nothing is written at a path outside the repository however that path reached the writing.
A run may gate and report leaving no file behind.
A run may gate and report leaving no loose object behind.
Gating without writing and writing without gating are refused together.
The index is reached only to keep that index.
Checks that will not load refuse the change.
Only writing without gating carries past the checks that will not load.
Why the checks would not load is said in the answer and in the commit.
A change naming a page to draft onto is kept there rather than landed.
A path taken away that something still imports refuses the change unwritten.
A path taken away beside the edits dropping its imports is written.
A path taken away is weighed against its importers whatever the change kind.
A path taken away that is a folder is taken away as a folder.
A subagent's page taken away leaves the edits kept beside it on that subagent's seat.
Those edits move before the uncommitted files beside that page are swept.
A landing refused after that move leaves what moved reachable from the seat.
A change kept beside a page to draft onto moves nothing off any page.
A refusal answered here carries no saying of its own.
A refusal carries whatever the caller folding it has to say alongside it.
A refusal answered here states the code that refusal exits with.
A change the checks refused is a fault of the data.
A change is judged over its own files rather than over the index answers it carries.
Those answers are named on the change as the files carried beside the ones judged.

definition: a change judged against one commit and then written and committed onto it, or refused whole
